candidate.text:
PROPOSED; not confirmed or implemented. Scope: uncertainty around a supplied differentiable estimating-equation point estimate, not selection of the outcome model or estimand. Input contract: fitted coefficient vector theta; each included person's unnormalised estimating contribution u_i(theta), including any weights used by that same fit; the Jacobian bread A = -sum_i d u_i(theta)/d theta evaluated at theta; and one valid district ID per included person. Districts are the independent units. Let G be the number of distinct contributing districts and U_g = sum of u_i over people in district g. For G >= 40, use V = A^{-1} [sum_g U_g U_g^T] A^{-T}; all sums use the same unnormalised convention. Proposed implementation convention is the uncorrected asymptotic sandwich, with no G/(G-1) or other finite-sample multiplier. For a scalar coefficient j, SE_j = sqrt(V_jj), and report a two-sided 95% normal Wald interval theta_j +/- 1.959963984540054*SE_j. For an explicitly reported exponentiated coefficient, exponentiate both endpoints of its coefficient-scale interval; this rule does not define inference for marginal risks or other derived estimands. The source supports the clustered method and >=40 applicability regime; the formula, no-correction and Wald conventions are explicit proposals for reproducibility, not additional claims about the source.
At the currently declared G=60, apply district clustering. Do not treat people as independent or substitute ordinary model-based uncertainty. If a subsequent fit has G<40 (including 39), missing/ambiguous district IDs, a noninvertible bread, nonfinite scores/covariance, or an invalid negative variance, stop this uncertainty calculation and open the relevant assessment; do not clip, silently drop records, or fall back to ordinary errors. G=40 satisfies the supplied note's stated threshold. Report the point estimator identifier, contributing G, cluster unit, sandwich formula, correction convention and CI construction with the eventual analysis. No existing formal F definition is consumed: this is a standalone uncertainty-function contract, with dependencies=[]; the eventual fit must supply its own explicit estimator/score inputs. No data calculation or model approval is implied.

candidate.text:
PROPOSED DEFAULT: six calendar months; not confirmed or implemented. Decision scope is a lag filter of already eligible follow-up contributions, not a redefinition of cohort entry, outcomes or the baseline model. Input contract for each person is the original unlagged follow-up-origin calendar date T0, valid dated events, and existing at-risk calendar dates or intervals with their original censoring/end rules. The proposal computes L_m by adding m calendar months directly to T0; preserve day of month when valid, otherwise clamp once to the destination month's last day. For the default m=6, retain only originally eligible time and events on or after L_6, intersecting the original at-risk set with [L_6, infinity). Thus dates before L_6 are excluded, an otherwise eligible event exactly on L_6 is included, and original endpoint/censoring and tie conventions still govern whether the contribution was eligible. Do not reset the analysis time origin to L_m, revive a person after an earlier terminal event, turn an early event into an event at L_m, or count an empty intersection. A person whose original at-risk set ends before L_m contributes no eligible post-lag time/events. Missing/invalid origin or event/interval dates are a data-check blocker, not a reason to impute an origin or silently choose a different lag. The calendar-month/clamp/exact-threshold conventions are proposed implementation decisions, not statements found in the source.
COMPLETE ALTERNATIVE for the same review decision: m=12 with exactly the same input contract, direct calendar-month addition, end-of-month clamp, on-or-after threshold, original time scale, at-risk-set intersection and error handling; replace every L_6 by L_12. Example with T0=2026-01-15: L_6=2026-07-15 and L_12=2027-01-15; otherwise eligible contributions on 2026-10-15 are retained by six months and excluded by twelve. Exact-threshold contributions are eligible under the matching option and the preceding day is excluded. For T0=2023-08-31, L_6=2024-02-29; for T0=2024-02-29, L_12=2025-02-28. A future event between thresholds must follow the chosen fixed rule, even though the current project reports zero events in months 6-12. Six months retains more usable information; twelve months removes a longer potentially reverse-causal interval but loses time and possibly events. No quantitative reduction in bias is asserted. No formal F definition is consumed by this standalone lag-transform contract (dependencies=[]); the eventual cohort specification must supply its declared original eligibility/time inputs. Human review must select six months or revise this candidate to the fully specified twelve-month alternative before formal confirmation.

Boundary review covers exact threshold, preceding day, end-of-month/leap-day clamping, an interval event distinguishing options, early at-risk termination and missing input dates.
review_packet.common_practice: The supplied lag-design note permits both six- and twelve-month exclusion windows and does not universally prefer either. It identifies information retention and potential reverse-causation removal as competing considerations.
review_packet.default: Recommended answer for review: the complete six-calendar-month candidate, because it retains more information under the stated objective. Equally admissible source-supported alternative: the complete twelve-calendar-month rule in the same candidate, with a longer potential reverse-causation interval removed and less time/events retained. Human choice remains required.
review_packet.departure_check: Neither option departs from the supplied note. Direct calendar-month addition, threshold inclusion, preserved origin and risk-set intersection are explicit proposed conventions needed to make both options operational; they are not attributed to the source. No current event-count coincidence is used to collapse the choice.
review_packet.project_reason: Six months addresses a lag exclusion while giving priority to the declared information-retention objective. Choosing twelve instead places greater priority on a longer possible reverse-causation interval; the supplied evidence cannot quantify which yields less total bias or better precision.
